From 19 August 2026, Scottish parliamentary constituencies used in Stat-Xplore were updated to reflect the latest (2026) boundaries as statistics were routinely refreshed in line with their publication schedules. For statistics that did not previously include a Scottish parliamentary constituency variable, one was added by default as part of the standardised offering for administrative geographies across all appropriate Stat-Xplore datasets. Further updates will be added to this section.

2.6. Get involved in the Explore Government Statistics Discovery

As part of the Government Statistical Service’s Strength in Numbers strategy, which includes an ambition to explore the feasibility of a cross-government dissemination platform for official statistics, DWP is participating in a pilot to share learning from the development and operation of the Department for Education’s ‘Explore Education Statistics’ dissemination platform.

The pilot team is undertaking a discovery project to better understand the needs of users of government statistics. This includes identifying who uses official statistics, how they access and use them, and the extent to which current statistical outputs meet their needs.

The project will also explore how official statistics could be made available through a shared cross-government platform, drawing on user feedback and existing best practice. If you use any government statistics, the pilot team would welcome your views. Register to take part via the sign-up form.

3. Confirmed changes coming to statistics

The following changes have been announced publicly and are summarised in the following table. Please see the relevant statistics release for more details.

Publication Details of development User requirement Date

The employment of disabled people Include variable about all reasons for economic inactivity. There has been increased interest in economic inactivity. 4 November 2026 – For more information please see The employment of disabled people collection page.

The employment of disabled people Employment and unemployment duration. Will provide additional insights into how disabled people experience employment (e.g. whether they move in and out of employment more often) and unemployment (e.g. for how long they remain unemployed compared with non-disabled people). 4 November 2026 – For more information please see The employment of disabled people collection page.

The employment of disabled people New strategic geographic boundaries (Mayoral Combined Authority and NHS Integrated Care Board). Statistics based on these geographies (Mayoral Combined Authority and NHS Integrated Care Board) are useful for strategy teams in relation to work and health programmes implementation and monitoring. 4 November 2026 – For more information please see The employment of disabled people collection page.

The employment of disabled people Alternative Disability Employment Gap (DEG) measures – prevalence-adjusted and age-adjusted. The disability employment gap is a key indicator of disability-related labour market inequality. In the last year, there has been discussion about whether the non-adjusted DEG (employment rate for non-disabled people minus rate for disabled people) is a useful measure. 4 November 2026 – For more information please see The employment of disabled people collection page.

Strategic need for NEET flows and increased understanding for reasons for being NEET. 4 November 2026 – For more information please see The employment of disabled people collection page.

Universal Credit Low Income statistics New quarterly statistics. Will provide local level data (local authority level and below) on poverty rates for families receiving Universal Credit in Great Britain. External recommendation to develop measures of income-based poverty from administrative data from the Office for Statistics Regulation. Many local authorities are very keen to have timely estimates of poverty for their area (including ward level estimates). 17 November 2026 – for more information please see the Households Below Average Income (HBAI) collection page.

Discretionary Housing Payments (DHP) statistics Need for a Wales-only publication, following the end of DHPs being delivered in England. DHPs are no longer delivered in England since April 2026. December 2026 - For more information, please see the Discretionary Housing Payments statistics collection page.

Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) and Jobseekers Allowance (JSA) Ethnicity: Collection of ethnicity data for working age claimants outside of Universal Credit (UC) (new style ESA and JSA) was suspended in September 2025 until a new platform is delivered to receive New Style claims and collect the required claimant data. As a result, ethnicity measures of the JSA and ESA caseloads published within these statistics were suspended from the November 2025 release onwards, until the new collection is underway and completion of the ethnicity field in the JSA and ESA caseloads has passed the minimum 70% threshold. This means that JSA and ESA data to February 2025 (released in August 2025) is the latest available time point where ethnicity breakdowns are available on Stat-Xplore.

State Pension (SP): To ensure accurate reporting, a temporary methodological solution has been applied to the data for May 2025 onwards to fully capture all SP cases, including those migrated to the Get Your SP (GYSP) service from the legacy platform. This means the statistics for May 2025 reflect the complete caseload, with no undercount.

Quarterly SP statistics for November 2024 and February 2025 contain a known undercount. During this period, approximately 5,000 to 6,000 cases (less than 0.05% of the total caseload) were migrated from the Pension Strategy Computer System (PSCS) to GYSP. However, due to the way GYSP data is compiled, these migrated cases were not yet visible in standard datastores and therefore were not included in the statistics.

While statistics for November 2024 and February 2025 remain unchanged, the temporary solution ensures that migrated cases are now included from May 2025 onwards. A permanent fix is in development to allow future statistics to capture all migrated cases without relying on tactical adjustments.

Jobseekers Allowance (JSA) Methodology Improvement: DWP Statisticians have identified that a subset of inactive JSA claims have been contributing to the caseload. A methodological improvement has been applied for August 2025 data onwards which will remove these inactive cases. As such, users can expect to see a decrease primarily in the Nil and Unknown payment counts. There is a caseload reduction in August 2025 of 13,000 (16.4%) attributable to the change in methodology.

Find more information on all of the above on the Annual DWP Benefits Statistics Compendium collection page.

Maternity Allowance (MA) suspension: Suspension of MA statistics from the August 2024 statistical release. Find more information on the MA collection page.

Economic labour market status of individuals aged 50 and over Due to the ongoing challenges with response rates and levels, Labour Force Survey-based labour market statistics will be badged as Official Statistics in Development until further review. This is in line with the letter from the Office for Statistics Regulation (OSR). Find more information on the latest release.

Family Resources Survey (FRS) Issue with the variable EDUCQUAL. This variable is used to present estimates of household food security status and household food bank usage, by educational attainment of head of household. These estimates were not available in the March 2024 publication. Investigation and corrective work during 2024 together with the ONS, means that EDUCQUAL data for 2022 to 2023 and 2023 to 2024 is now of the quality needed and tables have been published as 9.6 and 9.18 for 2023 to 2024. Investigation of past-year interview records shows that the EDUCQUAL issue also affects the 2021 to 2022 and 2020 to 2021 survey years (when it was known as DVHIQUAL). The corrected values for 2021 to 2022 are incorporated in the March 2026 release. The updated 2020 to 2021 values will be included in the new dataset scheduled for publication in March 2027. Prior years will not be adjusted, due to the data deletion policy under the governance of UK GDPR. Find more information on the FRS collection page.

This will also affect the onwardly derived CTANNUAL and CTAMT variables. However, the impact of this error is minimal and should not affect the use of the data.
